headline: Elected Susan Boucher as chair and filled three other officer posts; approved July 23 minutes and a draft proclamation for Commissioner Waldron.
summary: Commissioners agreed to strike Section O from the bylaws in the next update. They discussed questions about other bylaw sections, which staff will clarify before any vote. They also talked about outreach events, including a booth at the Branching Out Together event on August 21, 2026.
decisions: Approved Susan Boucher as Chair, with 5 votes in favor.
Approved John Kaligandis as Vice Chair, with 5 votes in favor.
Approved Thomas Palangas as Secretary, with 5 votes in favor.
Approved Lauren Zielinski as Treasurer, with 5 votes in favor.
Approved the July 23, 2026 meeting minutes, with all members in favor.
Agreed to strike Section O from the bylaws in the next update.
Approved the draft proclamation honoring Commissioner Waldron, with minor edits.

plain_text:
MANCHESTER CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
c/o City of Manchester Planning and Community Development Department 
One City Hall Plaza 
Manchester, NH 03101 
(603) 624-6450 
pcd@manchesternh.gov 
 
  
MEETING MINUTES 
of the   
MANCHESTER CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
           
August 19, 2026 – 6:00 PM 
Walter Stiles Room 
2nd Floor 
Manchester City Hall 
One City Hall Plaza 
 
Commission Members Present:          Susan Boucher 
John Kaligandis 
Jennifer MacLaren 
Thomas Palangas 
      Lauren Zielinski 
      Levent Akinci, Alternate 
      *Patrick Chabot (Non-voting) 
 
 Commission Members Absent:          None 
 
 Staff Present:     Kristin Bixby, Senior Planner 
 
 
I. Call to Order. 
The meeting was called to order by Commissioner Boucher at 6:00 PM. 
 
II. Roll. 
Five members and one  alternate member of the Commission are present, constituting a 
quorum. Commissioner Akinci is promoted to a full voting member.  
 
Commissioner Chabot , who has been confirmed for appointment by the Board of Mayor 
and Aldermen, has attended this meeting but has not yet been sworn- in by the City Clerk’s 
office. Accordingly, Commissioner Chabot did not officially vote on any agenda items this 
evening. 
 
III. Organizational Meeting: Membership Introductions and Election of Officers. 
     Membership Introductions: 
i. Why were you interested in joining the Commission?  
ii. What skills/background knowledge do you bring with you?  
iii. What would you like to see accomplished over the course of your term? 
iv. Would you like to be considered for any of the officer positions (Chair, Vice 
Chair, Secretary, Treasurer)?
Conservation Commission; August 19, 2026  Page | 2 
 
All members respond to the questions. Commissioner Boucher expresses interest in chairing 
the Commission, while Commissioner Kaligandis expresses interest in Vice Chair. 
Commissioner Palangas said he was willing to be designated as Secretary for the purpose of 
site visits or as otherwise needed, as the majority of the minutes will now be done by municipal 
staff. Commissioners Zielinski and MacLaren both volunteer to take on the Treasurer role, if 
needed. 
 
Election of Officers: 
Commissioner Boucher opens the organizational meeting. 
 
Commissioner MacLaren nominates Commissioner Boucher for Chair, seconded by 
Commissioner Kaligandis. 
 
There are no other nominations. 
 
Vote in f avor of Susan Boucher  as Chair:  MacLaren, Kaligandis, Akinci, Palangas, and 
Zielinski. Vote passed. Commissioner Boucher is voted in as Chair. 
 
Commissioner Zielinski nominates Commissioner Kaligandis for Vice Chair, seconded by 
Commissioner Palangas. 
 
There are no other nominations. 
 
Vote in favor of John Kaligandis  for Vice Chair: Zielinski, Palangas, Akinci, Boucher, and 
MacLaren. Vote passed. Commissioner Kaligandis is voted in as Vice Chair. 
 
Commissioner Kaligandis nominates Commissioner Palangas  for Secretary, seconded by 
Chair Boucher. 
 
There are no other nominations. 
  
Vote in favor of Thomas Palangas  as Secretary: Kaligandis, Boucher, Akinci, MacLaren, and 
Zielinski. Vote passed. Commissioner Palangas is voted in as Secretary. 
 
Commissioner Kaligandis nominates current Treasurer, Commissioner Zielinski, for 
Treasurer, seconded by Commissioner MacLaren.  
 
There are no other nominations. 
 
Vote in favor of  Lauren Zielinski for Treasurer: Kaligandis, MacLaren, Akinci, Boucher, and 
Palangas. Vote passed. Commissioner Zielinski is voted in as Treasurer. 
 
Chair Boucher ends the organizational meeting and begins the regular meeting. 
 
IV. Discussion of Conservation Commission Bylaws. 
Commissioners take a minute to review their Bylaws, which were last updated in 2022.  
 
There is an agreement that they no longer feel the requirement of badgers to be necessary and 
the section  [Section O ] should be struck for the next update of the Bylaws. They briefly 
discussed other alternatives to have their identities verified if called into question during a site 
visit, which included always having their own personal means of identification (driver’s 
license, etc), pointing people to the Conservation Commission page of the website that will 
have their name listed, and by carrying around Kristin Bixby’s business cards or otherwise 
telling them to call the Planning Department to verify that they are an active commissioner.
Conservation Commission; August 19, 2026  Page | 3 
 
The Commissioners also had a few questions about some language that Ms. Bixby will be 
looking to clarify before they decide on voting to change the language. In the Meetings  section 
of the bylaws, a subsection item [ F.5.] reads, “The Commission may suspend any of its rules 
during a meeting by majority vote .” The Commissioners would like to seek some clarification 
on the parameters of that item, and also would like to know if they could potentially strike that 
language. There was also some discussion on changing the language regarding the role of the 
Treasurer, as it currently mentions that they are “ responsible for recording all property 
acquired, owned, and dispensed by the Commission”  [C.1.d]. However, the Commission does 
not own any property and is really only ever charged with easement monitoring duties of City-
owned land, as designated  by the Board of Mayor and Aldermen. They would also like some 
clarification as to the protocol of who can run the meeting as Chair Pro Tempore in the off 
chance that the Chair, Vice Chair, and Secretary are not in attendance. More generally, they 
would like to provide more clarity in their bylaws regarding whose responsibility it would be, if 
any, to designate a Chair Pro Tempore in their absence or whether it should just go to a vote.  
 
V. Discussion on Conservation Commission Outreach Initiatives. 
Commissioner Akinci mentions that he will have a booth at the Branching Out Together event 
on Friday, August 21, 2026, for both the Friends of the Piscataquog River and the Conservation 
Commission. The Commissioners discussed that there should be more thought to putting 
together some general information about them and what they do for these types of events. 
Commissioner MacLaren offered to create something on Canva for Levent prior to Friday.  
 
Commissioner MacLaren volunteered to contact the Millyard Museum about having another 
outreach event that discusses the history of the Piscataquog and Merrimack rivers, the role they 
played in Manchester’s development, and how we can better protect them moving forward. 
This would be a good outreach event for colder months as it will not be weather -dependent. 
There was also a discussion about scheduling another fishways tour around April or May of 
2027, and scheduling a Cedar Swamp Tour that does not end up being too close to the Fourth 
of July or Father’s Day. 
 
VI. Review of Prior Meeting Minutes. 
July 23, 2026 meeting minutes are reviewed. Commissioner MacLaren  moves to approve the 
meeting minutes. Commissioner Akinci seconds the motion. Motion passes with all in favor. 
 
VII. Staff Update. 
Ms. Bixby acknowledges the newest member, Patrick Chabot . With the addition of 
Commissioner Chabot, but also the resignation of Commissioner Waldron, that still leaves the 
Commission short one full member and one alternate member. 
 
Ms. Bixby also passes around a draft of the proclamation that she and Commissioner Boucher 
had collaborated on and are planning to submit to the Mayor’s Office as a way to honor 
Commissioner Waldron’s time on the Commission. The commissioners all approved of the 
draft with minor edits. 
 
VIII. Other Business. 
No other business was discussed at the meeting.
Conservation Commission; August 19, 2026  Page | 4 
 
IX. Adjournment. 
Commissioner Palangas moves to adjourn the meeting. Commissioner MacLaren seconds the 
motion.  Motion passes with all in favor.  
 
The meeting is adjourned at 6:44 PM. 
 
 
 
 
ATTEST:   
                 
Susan Boucher 
                 Chair, Manchester Conservation Commission 
 
 
 
 
 
APPROVED BY THE MANCHESTER CONSERVATION COMMISSION:  October 28, 2026 
 
 
Minutes prepared by: Kristin Bixby, Senior Planner
